Let me see if I am able to list all of the things that I love about Arch.

1.) Arch is a rolling release, and updates come directly from upstream (generally without modifications), so (after some testing to make sure that they are sufficiently stable) an Arch install is always up-to-date with the most up-to-date packages available in any distro of Linux.

2.) AUR (Arch User Repository), which is a huge user-maintained repo of PKGBUILD files, which allows one to download, build from source, and install a vast array of software not found in the official repositories, either using one of the many AUR helpers, or manually.

3.) Unofficial Arch Repositories are user created and maintained binary repositories with a wide and diverse array of software packages.

4.) Pacman (package manager) is the fastest Linux package manager in any Linux distro.

5.) Pretty much any software that exists in any Linux distro exists in the Official Repositories, the Unofficial Repositories, and the AUR, or can easily be installed in Arch, even if it does not exist in those repos. We're talking a MASSIVE array of software packages.

6.) ABS (Arch Build System) is a repo of PKGBUILD files for every package in the Official repositories, that allows one to download, modify to one's requirements, build from source, and install these specially modified versions easily. It is similar to ports collection in the BSDs or Portage in Gentoo.

7.) Arch is extremely simple, logical, and efficient, and the base install allows one to build a system EXACTLY the way one desires or needs, without unnecessary packages and fluff.

8.) The Arch Wiki, which is bar-none the absolute best wiki in any Linux distro. There is a massive amount of information here to do just about anything one would like to do with Arch.

9.) The Arch Forums are a truly excellent resource for trouble shooting and connecting with the Arch community. There are also Arch IRC channels.

10.) Arch is 100% maintained and improved by a wide and diverse global volunteer community, with no connections to any corporation, and no intention to go in that direction.

11.) The manner in which kernels are handled in Arch is the simplest and most elegant I've seen in any distro, as is the mkinitcpio build system for their initramfs files.

12.) Given that Arch has few distribution-specific modifications, most commands, setups, and scripts that will work in vanilla Linux will work in Arch, with little to no tweaking.

Those are just a few off the top of my head. There are more. When I got into Arch, and continued to dive deeper into it, I continued to fall deeper and deeper in love with it. At this point, I could not even imagine ever wanting to go to another distro again.

“Besides the advantage of being armed, which the Americans possess over the people of almost every other nation, the existence of subordinate governments, to which the people are attached, and by which the militia officers are appointed, forms a barrier against the enterprises of ambition, more insurmountable than any which a simple government of any form can admit of.
